what: Investigated whether the DLSS-NR path drops camera jitter offset (hypothesis for pre-SR blur). Confirmed at code level: (1) every OptiScaler upscaler feature reads NVSDK_NGX_Parameter_Jitter_Offset_X/Y from the incoming NGX param block at evaluate (FSR2/2.1.2/3.1, FFX, XeSS across Dx11/Dx12/Vk; IFeature.cpp:241) -- so the game reliably supplies it and the codebase treats it as a required temporal input; (2) DlssNr_Dx12.cpp EvaluateInternal reads DLSS_Render_Subrect_Dimensions and MV_Scale_X/Y from that same block (lines ~3186-3193) but never reads Jitter.Offset.X/Y; (3) the NR forwarder (dlssnr_forwarder.cpp dlssnr_call_evaluate / dlssnr_vk_evaluate) sets ~30 DLSSNR.* params, none jitter-related; (4) grep -ri jitter over OptiScaler/dlssnr and OptiScaler/shaders/dlssnr = zero hits. NR model is NGX feature id 18 (DLSS-D/Ray Reconstruction), whose temporal reconstruction needs subpixel jitter to align history. Residual unknown: retail nvngx_dlssnr.dll's full 61-name DLSSNR.* vocabulary not dumpable here (only the forwarder binary is in-repo), so the exact model-side slot name is unconfirmed. Impact: post-SR placement feeds NR a resolved/de-jittered image so the gap is near-invisible; pre-SR feeds raw jittered render-res color, so NR history reprojection is misaligned by the per-frame jitter delta -> softening/smearing. Matches the design doc's stated reason for forcing RR post-SR; the plain-SR pre path has the same contract gap and was not guarded.

what: Dumped the retail nvngx_dlssnr.dll string table (v310.8.0, 165 MB; copies found in game folders + ~/Downloads + ~/AppData/Local/RHI, all 61 DLSSNR.* names identical). Result kills the jitter-parameter Fix Shape: the model exposes exactly 61 DLSSNR.* param names and NONE is jitter-related. The substring 'jitter' occurs 0 times in the whole binary; no 'Jitter.Offset' (NGX SR name), no halton/phase/subpixel, no camera/view/clip matrix params at all. The full input surface is: resources (Color/Depth/MVec/Output/UI/UIAlpha/Backbuffer/ControlMask/BidirectionalDistortionField) + per-resource subrects, Enabled/Width/Height, DepthInverted, Reset, MVecScaleX/Y, Hint.Render.Preset, Intensity, LocalStructureStrength, LocalToneStrength, SkinStructureStrength, Style, UICorrection, UseAutoMask, ScalingRatio. So the ONLY channel for frame-to-frame pixel correspondence is the MVec texture. Conclusion: DLSS-NR (feature id 18) has no jitter input because it is designed to run SR-fused, where the SR half resolves jitter; its native contract is display-res post-jitter-resolve color = the post-SR placement. Pre-SR feeds it jittered render-res color with no way to inform it -> softening is intrinsic, not a missing setFloat. Confirmed root cause (High confidence). No clean fix via a jitter param. Only technically-available fix: bake the per-frame jitter delta into the MVec texture handed to NR (a synthetic jittered-MV / jitter-cancellation compute pass, cf. FFX_FSR2_ENABLE_MOTION_VECTORS_JITTER_CANCELLATION and XeFG JITTERED_MV already in this repo) -- bigger change than discussed, and speculative (unknown whether the model does jitter-aware reprojection at all; may be design case (c) = accepts the error, built for post-SR). Did not implement; surfaced options to user for a decision.

what: Fixed a third SGSR1 bug, found from a new user report: 'it becomes blurred when i choose neuto replace or hybrid replace' (DlssNrReversibleMode 2/4) with model resolution below 100%. Root cause: SGSR1 upscales the model answer/proxy textures, which under Neutwo/Hybrid mapping are LinearToSrgb(NeutwoEncode(normalized)) or LinearToSrgb(HybridEncode(normalized)) -- an extra compressive curve on top of gamma, squashing local contrast hardest in highlights. sgsr1.hlsl's edge detector compares neighbouring green-channel texels against a fixed kEdgeThreshold=8/255 (Qualcomm's constant, tuned for ordinary gamma content), which rarely trips against the extra-compressed curve, so the pass silently fell back to plain bilinear far more than intended. Composed modes (0/1/3) mask this because the resolve's ratio/hue blend leans on the native original for most spatial detail; Replace modes (2/4) take the SGSR1 output completely raw, exposing the softness directly -- matching the report. User chose the fix direction via AskUserQuestion ('decode before SGSR1, re-encode after' over threshold-scaling or leave-as-limitation). Implemented: ported Neutwo/Hybrid encode/decode math into sgsr1.hlsl, added ReversibleMode/Passthrough to its Params cbuffer (replacing the _Pad placeholder) and to SGSR1_Dx12::Dispatch()'s signature, sourced from resolveParams at both call sites in DlssNr_Dx12.cpp. DecodeDomain/EncodeDomain (exact, hue-preserving, full-RGB peak-channel curve) wrap the base colour sample and the final written colour; DecodeGreenScalar (single-channel approximation, since GatherGreen only returns one channel) feeds only the edge-vote/weight heuristics, never the written colour. All identity when ReversibleMode==0 or Passthrough!=0, so the already-working SoftKnee/Off case is untouched. what: Implemented the linear-light downsample fix proposed after mapping DLSS-NR's render paths (docs/DLSSNR-SIGNAL-PATH.html). Added DecodeProxyToLinear/EncodeLinearToProxy (dlssnr.hlsl, after HybridDecode) mirroring the encode pass's exact Passthrough/ReversibleMode branching, wrapping each tap and the final average.
